Build a signed systemd-boot A/B release with a verified root from an existing
root filesystem.

## Inputs

| Name                 | Kind      | Description                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kernel`             | file      | Target Linux kernel image.                                                                                        |
| `initrd`             | file      | Initrd implementing the core verified-root boot contract.                                                         |
| `rootfs`             | directory | Prepared root filesystem implementing the core verified-root boot contract.                                       |
| `boot-certificate`   | file      | PEM-encoded RSA X.509 certificate for signing EFI boot artifacts.                                                 |
| `bundle-certificate` | file      | Single PEM-encoded RSA X.509 end-entity signer certificate issued directly by the trusted root. No intermediates. |

## Parameters

| Name               | Default      | Description                                                                                                             |
| ------------------ | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `architecture`     | **Required** | Target architecture: amd64 or arm64. Must match the system architecture.                                                |
| `cmdline-extra`    | `""`         | Additional authenticated kernel arguments.                                                                              |
| `panic-timeout`    | `10`         | Kernel panic reboot delay in seconds. Zero leaves the system stopped.                                                   |
| `boot-timeout`     | `0`          | systemd-boot menu timeout in seconds.                                                                                   |
| `signing-time`     | `""`         | Signing time as Unix seconds in a string. Empty uses the build source epoch.                                            |
| `config-size`      | `0`          | ESP capacity in bytes. Zero reserves three copies of its current files, uses at least 256 MiB, and rounds up to 64 MiB. |
| `root-compression` | `"none"`     | SquashFS compression of the root filesystem, such as zstd or xz, or none.                                               |
| `disk-size`        | `0`          | Factory disk capacity in bytes. Zero sizes the disk from its partitions.                                                |
| `secondary-config` | `false`      | Reserve an empty secondary configuration partition with the same capacity as the ESP.                                   |

## Secrets

Required secret bindings: `boot-key`, `bundle-key`. Secret changes invalidate
cached outputs.

## Execution

Composes other rules into a build graph.

## Behavior

Build an EFI A/B release with a verified root from an existing root filesystem,
kernel, and initrd. The composition builds a SquashFS root filesystem, appends
dm-verity authentication data, embeds the root hash and image geometry in a
Unified Kernel Image (UKI), signs the UKI and systemd-boot, and assembles a
factory GPT disk and signed Rugix update bundle.

The required `architecture` is `amd64` or `arm64` and must match the kernel. The
root filesystem supplies `etc/os-release`. The initrd must implement the
[core verified-root boot contract](../../recipes/debian-verified-root/); custom
distributions can implement the same contract independently.

The factory disk contains the EFI System Partition (ESP) with the initial
`rugix-a.efi` UKI and the A system partition with the combined root image. The
ESP also carries the bootstrap marker and becomes Rugix Ctrl's configuration
partition at `/run/rugix/mounts/config`. On first boot, Rugix Ctrl preserves the
ESP, expands the system capacity, creates an empty B system partition, and
creates data in the remaining drive space according to the root filesystem's
bootstrap plan. The platform setup recipe defaults both system slots to at least
4 GiB. [The EFI layout rule](../layout-efi-ab/) describes the factory and
completed layouts.

Factory sizing requires no size settings:

- Root: SquashFS sized to its contents, followed by verity data.
- ESP: reserve three copies of the current boot files, use at least 256 MiB, and
  round up to 64 MiB.
- Disk: fit the factory partition layout automatically.

`root-compression` selects the SquashFS compression of the root filesystem and
defaults to `none`, which helps delta updates find unchanged data. Select a
compressor such as `zstd` or `xz` for smaller images.

`config-size` and `disk-size` are optional factory capacity overrides. The
bootstrap plan controls deployed system capacities and data allocation. Once
bootstrapped, future payloads must fit the deployed slots. `signing-time` is
Unix seconds encoded as a string; empty uses the build source epoch.

The bundle delivers combined `system.img` and signed `boot.efi` payloads to
Rugix Ctrl slots named `system` and `boot`. The consuming root filesystem must
configure those slots as corresponding A/B boot groups.

| Output        | Contents                                                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `image`       | Factory disk                                                        |
| `bundle`      | Signed update bundle                                                |
| `uki`         | Signed UKI                                                          |
| `bootloader`  | Signed systemd-boot executable                                      |
| `root-hash`   | Root hash embedded in the UKI                                       |
| `hash-offset` | Byte offset of the appended hash area, as decimal text              |
| `data-size`   | SquashFS length in bytes before padding and hashes, as decimal text |

Boot certificate enrollment and firmware trust configuration happen separately.

Supply one PEM-encoded RSA certificate as `bundle-certificate`. The bundle
embeds only this signer certificate, without intermediates. Issue it directly
from the root that Rugix Ctrl trusts. The signer must not be a CA certificate.

## Customize Boot Settings

Set `cmdline-extra` to supply kernel arguments, such as consoles and log levels.
It defaults to an empty string. The `panic-timeout` parameter defaults to 10
seconds; zero disables automatic reboot after a panic. Verified-root arguments
remain supplied by the composition.

Set `boot-timeout` to control the systemd-boot menu timeout in seconds. For
example:

```toml
parameters.cmdline-extra = "console=ttyS0,115200n8 loglevel=4"
parameters.panic-timeout = 30
parameters.boot-timeout = 5
```

## Example

For example, assemble prepared artifacts:

```toml
uses = "core/image-efi-verified"
inputs.rootfs = { path = "prepared-root" }
inputs.kernel = { path = "kernel" }
inputs.initrd = { path = "initrd" }
inputs.boot-certificate = { path = "keys/boot.crt" }
inputs.bundle-certificate = { path = "keys/bundle.crt" }
secrets.boot-key = { path = "keys/boot.key" }
secrets.bundle-key = { path = "keys/bundle.key" }
parameters.architecture = "amd64"
```

Save the invocation as `build-rule.toml` and run
`./run-bakery bake rule build-rule.toml build/result`. For Debian roots,
[the Debian wrapper](../image-debian-efi-verified/) also selects a kernel and
generates its initrd.

## Secondary Configuration Partition

To reserve space for a replacement ESP, including systemd-boot, set
`parameters.secondary-config = true`. This adds an empty `config-secondary`
partition with the same capacity as `config`. Both config partitions precede the
system partitions, so `system-a`, `system-b`, and `data` use partition numbers
3, 4, and 5 after bootstrap.

Enable the matching recipe option in the root filesystem's layer:

```toml
[parameters."core/debian-efi-verified-setup"]
secondary_config = true
```

Use this option when provisioning a matching factory layout. Existing
installations need a separate partition-layout migration before receiving the
changed root configuration.

Custom roots must provide equivalent system and bootstrap configurations. The
[EFI layout rule](../layout-efi-ab/) describes the reserved partition. The
update bundle continues to update the root and UKI slots; updating and
activating a replacement ESP requires a separate operation.
